scenarios.name: S1: Cab Order Persistence across Crash
scenarios.description: Home all elevators, send elev1 a cab order to floor 4, kill it mid-journey, then reboot and verify the order is still served.

steps.message: Step 1: Verify all elevators are homed to floor 0.
Step 2: Inject cab order to floor 4 (index 3) for elev1.
Step 3: Wait for elev1 to start moving.
Step 4: Kill elev1 mid-journey.
Step 5: Reboot elev1.
Step 6: Verify elev1 resumes and completes the cab order at floor 4.
Step 7: Wait for elev1 to close doors and become idle.
Scenario completed successfully. Order fully processed.

scenarios.name: S2: Hall Order Survives Crash Within Broadcast Window
scenarios.description: Inject a hall order on elev1, kill elev1 after 600ms (before the second periodic broadcast fires reliably), and verify that elev2 or elev3 received the order via eager broadcast and serves it.

steps.message: Step 1: Verify all elevators are homed and idle.
Step 2: Inject HallUp at floor 2 into elev1's simulator.
Step 3: Wait 600ms — enough for eager broadcast, tight enough to test the crash window.
Step 4: Kill elev1. elev2 and elev3 must now serve the hall order.
Step 5: Verify a surviving elevator served or is serving the hall order at floor 2.
Step 6: Wait for serving elevator to finish (idle at floor 2).
Step 7: Verify logs confirm the hall order was placed and cleared.
Step 8: Restart elev1 to restore the cluster.
Step 9: Verify elev1 reconnects and stays idle — it must NOT re-serve the already-cleared order.
S2 complete: hall order survived crash-before-broadcast, served by surviving peer, elev1 reconnected cleanly.

scenarios.name: S3: Door Obstruction Handling
scenarios.description: Three-part test of the obstruction switch. Part A: obstruction holds the door open past the 3-second timer. Part B: releasing obstruction restarts the 3-second close timer rather than closing immediately. Part C: obstruction while moving stops the elevator and opens the door.

steps.message: === Part A: Basic obstruction hold ===
Step A1: Verify all elevators are homed and idle at floor 0.
Step A2: Inject hall_up at floor 1 and cab floor 1 on elev1 — guarantees elev1 serves the order.
Step A3: Wait for elev1 to arrive at floor 1 and open its door.
Step A4: Toggle obstruction ON — intercepts the running 3s door timer.
Step A6: Sleep 4s — the 3-second door timer must NOT close the door while obstructed.
Step A7: Toggle obstruction OFF.
Step A8: Verify the door closes and elev1 becomes idle within 8s.
=== Part B: Obstruction release followed by fresh order starts a new 3-second close timer ===
Step B1: Inject hall_up floor 1 to make elev1 open its door at floor 1.
Step B2: Wait for elev1 to be doorOpen at floor 1.
Step B3: Toggle obstruction ON — holds door open past the 3-second timer.
Step B4: Sleep 2s — obstruction is holding the door.
Step B5: Toggle obstruction OFF — door closes immediately (FSM quirk with goal=None).
Step B6: Inject cab floor 1 while elev1 is idle — re-opens door with a fresh 3s timer.
Step B7: Wait for elev1 to re-open door at floor 1 (fresh 3s timer started).
Step B8: Sleep 1.5s — fresh 3s timer is running, door must still be open. (1.5s leaves 500ms+ margin before the 3s timer fires.)
Step B9: Wait up to 6s for the 3-second timer to expire and the door to close.
=== Part C: Obstruction while moving stops the elevator and opens the door ===
Step C1: Inject hall_up floor 3 and cab floor 3 on elev1 to send it upward.
Step C2: Wait for elev1 to start moving.
Step C3: Toggle obstruction ON while elev1 is moving.
Step C4: Verify elev1 stops moving within 6s.
Step C5: Verify elev1 has opened its door (doorOpen).
Step C6: Toggle obstruction OFF.
Step C7: Verify elev1 eventually reaches floor 3 and completes the order.
=== Final log verification ===
S3 complete: obstruction hold, timer restart, and mid-motion stop all verified.

scenarios.name: S4: Directional Hall Order Clearing
scenarios.description: Three-part test of directional hall-order clearing. Part A: an up-travelling elevator clears only HallUp at floor 2, leaving HallDown for a second door-open cycle. Part B: a down-travelling elevator clears only HallDown at floor 1, leaving HallUp for a second cycle. Part C: log verification confirms two door-opens at each floor via [EVENT] counts (the FSM transitions through idle between them too fast for UDP polling to observe).

steps.message: === Part A: Up-travelling elevator clears HallUp only at floor 2 ===
Step A1: Verify all elevators homed and idle at floor 0.
Step A2: Kill elev2 and elev3 so only elev1 can serve orders.
Step A3: Inject hall_up floor 2, hall_down floor 2, and cab floor 2 on elev1.
Step A4: Verify elev1 starts moving upward.
Step A5: Verify elev1 arrives at floor 2 and opens door (first pass).

Step A6: Wait for elev1 to finish both door-opens at floor 2 and become idle. The FSM opens the door twice (once for HallUp direction=Up, once for HallDown direction=Stop after timer fires), but the transient idle between them is not observable via UDP. Allow up to 20s for the full double-open sequence to complete.
=== Part B: Down-travelling elevator clears HallDown only at floor 1 ===
Step B1: Inject hall_down floor 1, hall_up floor 1, and cab floor 1 on elev1 (from floor 2).
Step B2: Verify elev1 starts moving downward.
Step B3: Verify elev1 arrives at floor 1 and opens door (first pass).
Step B4: Wait for elev1 to finish both door-opens at floor 1 and become idle.
=== Part C: Log verification and cluster restoration ===
Step C1: Restart elev2 and elev3.
Step C2: Verify logs confirm directional clearing: two [EVENT] door_opened at floor 2 and two at floor 1, all four hall orders served and cleared.
S4 complete: directional hall-order clearing verified for both Up and Down directions.

scenarios.name: S5: Network Isolation — Disconnected Elevator Serves Existing and New Calls
scenarios.description: Three-part test of the spec requirement that a disconnected elevator must continue serving all active calls and accept new cab calls without requiring a restart. Part A: elev1 has hall (floor 1 and floor 2) and cab (floor 3) orders in its state before peers are killed; it must serve all three stops alone while isolated. Part B: a new cab call (floor 0) is injected while elev1 is isolated; it must react and serve it. Part C: peers are restarted and the cluster reforms cleanly with no spurious re-serves. Note: hall_up floor 3 does not exist — the top floor has no up button.

steps.message: === Part A: Serve pre-loaded orders while isolated ===
Step A1: Verify all elevators are homed and idle at floor 0.
Step A2: Inject hall_up at floor 1 on elev1's simulator.
Step A3: Inject hall_up at floor 2 on elev1's simulator. Note: hall_up floor 3 does not exist (top floor has no up button); floor 2 is the highest valid hall_up.
Step A4: Inject cab floor 3 on elev1 — a personal cab order at the top floor.
Step A5: Sleep 1s to let the eager broadcast propagate all three orders into elev1's SystemState before isolation begins.
Step A6: Kill elev2 and elev3 — simulating network isolation for elev1.
Step A7: Sleep 2s — peer-discovery timeout is 1500ms. elev1 must mark both peers dead and re-run the assigner as a solo node before we assert any behaviour.
Step A8: Verify elev1 starts moving — it must have self-assigned the pending orders.
Step A9: Wait for elev1 to arrive at floor 1 and open its door (first pre-loaded hall_up order). Non-asserting — transient state may be missed by polling.
Step A10: Wait for elev1 to close its door and start moving toward floor 2.
Step A11: Wait for elev1 to arrive at floor 2 and open its door (hall_up floor 2 order). Non-asserting — transient state may be missed by polling.
Step A12: Wait for elev1 to close its door and start moving toward floor 3.
Step A13: Wait for elev1 to arrive at floor 3 and open its door (cab order). Non-asserting — transient state may be missed by polling.
Step A14: Wait for elev1 to close its door and become idle at floor 3.
=== Part B: Accept new cab calls while isolated ===
Step B1: Inject cab floor 0 on elev1 while it is isolated at floor 3. The spec requires it to accept and serve new cab calls even while disconnected.
Step B2: Verify elev1 starts moving toward floor 0 within 8s.
Step B3: Verify elev1 arrives at floor 0 and opens its door — it served the new cab call while isolated.
Step B4: Wait for elev1 to become idle at floor 0.
=== Part C: Rejoin cluster without restart ===
Step C1: Restart elev2 and elev3. The spec says no manual reinitialization should be required after network loss — elev1 must rejoin automatically.
Step C2: Sleep 5s to allow peer discovery, state broadcasts, and cross-node merge to complete.
Step C3: Verify all three nodes are visible and stable — no phantom orders, no spurious movement.
Step C4: Sleep 3s then verify elev1 has not started moving spontaneously — no phantom order or spurious re-serve.
Step C5: Log verification — all orders served, no orders stuck, correct behaviour sequence.
S5 complete: isolated elevator served pre-loaded hall and cab orders, accepted a new cab call while disconnected, and rejoined the cluster cleanly without restart.

scenarios.name: S6: Dead Elevator Takeover Mid-Journey
scenarios.description: Verifies that when an elevator is killed while traveling to serve a hall order, the surviving peers detect the failure via peer-discovery timeout, re-assign the abandoned call via the hall-request assigner, and successfully serve the stranded order.

steps.message: S6 Part A: Home all elevators and inject a hall order to trigger movement.
S6 Part B: Kill elev1 mid-journey and wait for peer-discovery timeout.
S6 Part C: Verify a surviving elevator takes over and serves the stranded hall order.
S6 complete: surviving peer detected dead elevator, took over stranded hall order, and served it successfully.

scenarios.name: S7: Cab Isolation — Cab Orders Not Shared Between Nodes
scenarios.description: Verifies that cab orders are strictly local: only the elevator at the cab button's simulator reacts, while peers remain idle at floor 0 for the entire duration, proving cab_requests are never assigned to other nodes by the hall_request_assigner.

steps.message: S7 Part A: Home all elevators and inject a cab order on elev1 only.
S7 Part B: Verify peers ignored elev1's cab order and never left floor 0.
S7 complete: elev1 served its local cab order; elev2 and elev3 remained idle at floor 0, confirming cab isolation.

scenarios.name: S8: Simultaneous Hall Orders — Assigner Efficiency
scenarios.description: Verifies the hall_request_assigner distributes concurrent hall calls across multiple elevators. Two hall orders (floor 1 and floor 2) are injected simultaneously from different simulators. If both are cleared within 12 seconds it proves parallel dispatch: a single elevator serving them sequentially would require >12 seconds (travel + 2x door-open), so clearing both within 12s is only possible if two elevators worked in parallel.

steps.message: S8 Part A: Home all elevators and inject two simultaneous hall orders on different simulators.
S8 Part B: Verify all orders were served within the 12-second parallel execution window.
S8 complete: both hall orders cleared within 12 seconds, proving the assigner dispatched them to separate elevators in parallel.

scenarios.name: S9: Restart Loop with Order Injection — Chaos Resilience
scenarios.description: Verifies that rapid successive kills and restarts of one elevator (elev1) do not corrupt the distributed state OR lose orders. Orders (both hall and cab) are injected between each kill/restart cycle. Each restart generates a new boot_id and resets seq to 0; if merge_with handles boot_id epoch transitions incorrectly, stale network packets could override fresh state, producing phantom orders or losing real ones. After three chaos cycles with active orders, all orders must be served and the cluster must settle cleanly with no phantom movement.

steps.message: S9 Part A: Verify clean cluster state before inducing chaos.
S9 Iteration 1: Inject hall_up floor 1 and cab floor 2 on elev1 → kill elev1 → restart → verify orders survive.
Killing elev1 with pending orders (Iteration 1).
S9 Iteration 2: Inject hall_down floor 2 → kill elev1 mid-serve → restart → verify order survives.
Killing elev1 (may be moving or serving) (Iteration 2).
S9 Iteration 3: Inject cab floor 3 on elev1 → kill elev1 → restart → verify order survives.
Killing elev1 with pending cab order (Iteration 3).
S9 Part B: Allowing cluster to serve all pending orders and stabilize.
S9 Part C: Log verification — all orders served, no phantom orders.
S9 complete: three rapid restart cycles with active orders did not produce phantom orders or lose real orders. All hall and cab orders survived the restarts and were served. Cluster is stable.

scenarios.name: S10: The Rolling Blackout — Maximum Chaos Failover
scenarios.description: Tests the passing of cluster state memory across rolling failures. Multiple hall orders are injected into a healthy cluster, then nodes are killed one by one until only a single survivor remains holding the full world-view. A new node boots and syncs the pending orders from the survivor before the survivor is killed — the torch is passed. The cluster is then fully restored and we verify that no hall order was lost during the entire rolling blackout, as long as at least one node remained alive at all times.

steps.message: Part A — Setup: Verify all elevators are homed and idle at floor 0.
Injecting multiple orders: Hall Up Floor 2 (elev1), Hall Down Floor 3 (elev2), and Cab Floor 3 for elev1 (so elev1 must serve it after syncing).
Part B — First Wave of Failures: Killing elev1 and elev2. elev3 is the sole survivor.
Part C — The Torch Pass: Restarting elev1. It must sync the pending orders from elev3.
Killing elev3. elev1 is now the sole survivor.
Part D — Cluster Restoration: Restarting elev2 and elev3 to restore the cluster.
S10 complete: all hall orders survived the rolling blackout. The torch was passed successfully from elev3 to elev1, and the fully restored cluster confirmed zero order loss.

scenarios.name: S12: Emergency Stop — Motor Halts and Elevator Resumes
scenarios.description: Verifies the emergency stop button (key 'p'). Part A: pressing stop mid-motion halts the motor and transitions the elevator to idle. Part B: releasing stop allows the elevator to resume its goal and serve the pending order. Tests that the halt is immediate and that resumption happens via the normal assigner path without any data loss.

steps.message: === Part A: Emergency stop halts motor mid-motion ===
Step A1: Verify all elevators are homed and idle at floor 0.
Step A2: Inject cab floor 3 on elev1 — cab order guarantees only elev1 serves it.
Step A3: Wait for elev1 to start moving toward floor 3.

Step A4: Sleep 1s so elev1 is mid-journey, then press emergency stop. The simulator auto-releases the stop button after 200ms (btnDepressedTime_ms=200), so EmergencyStop(true) and EmergencyStop(false) are both fired within 200ms. The halt is too brief to observe via UDP polling, but the behaviour_sequence log check (Step B4) proves it happened.
=== Part B: Stop auto-releases after 200ms — elevator resumes automatically ===

Step B1: The simulator's btnDepressedTime_ms=200 means the stop button auto-releases 200ms after the press in Part A. The EmergencyStop(false) event fires automatically. With the fix, the release handler calls decide_next_order and fsm::step(goal), so elev1 resumes without any re-injection.
Step B2: Verify elev1 resumes moving toward floor 3 within 5s of the stop press.
Step B3: Verify elev1 eventually reaches floor 3 and opens its door — the cab order must be served.
Step B4: Log verification — cab order served, correct behaviour sequence.

S12 complete: emergency stop halted the motor immediately; the simulator auto-released the stop button after 200ms, triggering auto-resume via the fixed EmergencyStop(false) handler, and elev1 served the pending cab order without any re-injection.

scenarios.name: S11: Severe Packet Loss and Network Healing
scenarios.description: Verifies the system remains operational under 75% UDP packet loss. A hall order is injected while the network is severely degraded; elevators may enter a split-brain state and multiple may attempt to serve the order. Once the network heals, the cluster must merge state, globally clear the order, and stabilize without phantom orders or crashes.

steps.message: Part A: Verify all elevators homed before applying noise.
Applying 75% packet loss to UDP traffic.
Part B: Injecting Hall Down at Floor 2.
Waiting for any elevator to serve the order despite packet loss (split-brain may cause multiple to serve it).
Part C: Removing packet loss. The network is healing.
Verify cluster stabilizes and all elevators return to idle.
S11 complete: system survived 75% packet loss, served the order, and re-synchronized cleanly.

scenarios.name: S13: Two-Node Crash — Single Survivor Serves All Pending Hall Orders
scenarios.description: Verifies the single-survivor guarantee: two hall orders are injected simultaneously, then two of the three elevators are killed within the peer-discovery window. The sole surviving elevator must detect both peers as dead, re-run the assigner as a solo node, and serve both stranded hall orders without help. Tests the assigner's behaviour under maximum failure load and confirms hall epoch persistence across the double-crash.

steps.message: === Part A: Inject two hall orders with all three nodes alive ===
Step A1: Verify all elevators are homed and idle at floor 0.
Step A2: Inject hall_up floor 1 on elev1's simulator and hall_up floor 2 on elev2's simulator.
Step A3: Sleep 1s to let the eager broadcasts propagate both orders to all nodes.
=== Part B: Kill two nodes — elev3 is the sole survivor ===
Step B1: Kill elev1 and elev2 in rapid succession.
Step B2: Sleep 2.5s for peer-discovery timeout (1500ms) to expire for both dead nodes.
=== Part C: Verify elev3 serves both stranded hall orders alone ===
Step C1: Verify elev3 starts moving — it must have self-assigned both pending hall orders.
Step C2: Verify elev3 serves the floor 1 order (doorOpen or idle at floor 1). Non-asserting — transient state.
Step C3: Verify elev3 eventually serves the floor 2 order.
Step C4: Wait for elev3 to finish and become idle.
=== Part D: Restore cluster and verify no orders remain ===
S13 complete: single surviving elevator detected both peers as dead, self-assigned both pending hall orders, and served them alone. Cluster restored cleanly.

scenarios.name: SX-D: Bug Verification — Emergency Stop Release Does Not Auto-Resume
scenarios.description: Verifies that releasing the emergency stop button causes the elevator to automatically resume serving its pending order WITHOUT any re-injection. The bug: Event::EmergencyStop always calls fsm::step with goal=None, so on release (is_stopped=false) the elevator stays idle. The fix: on release, re-evaluate current_goal and pass it to fsm::step so the elevator resumes immediately.

steps.message: SX-D Step 1: Inject cab floor 3 on elev1 to send it upward.
SX-D Step 2: Press emergency stop mid-journey. The simulator auto-releases after 200ms, firing EmergencyStop(true) then EmergencyStop(false) automatically.
SX-D Step 3: Verify elev1 resumes moving automatically — the fix re-evaluates current_goal on EmergencyStop(false) and calls fsm::step with the goal.
SX-D Step 4: Verify elev1 reaches floor 3 and serves the cab order.
SX-D complete: emergency stop release auto-resumes pending order without re-injection.

scenarios.name: SX-B: Bug Verification — arrive_at_floor Corrupts Direction at Boundary Floors
scenarios.description: Verifies that arrive_at_floor does NOT call stop() at boundary floors 0 and 3, which would corrupt the direction before clear_order runs. Concrete test: elevator moving UP to floor 3 with HallDown at floor 3. Without the fix, stop() sets direction=Stop before clear_order, so the Stop-arm clears HallDown on the first door-open. With the fix, direction=Up is preserved and clear_order(Up) does NOT clear HallDown — requiring a second door-open via the Stop arm.

steps.message: SX-B Step 1: Inject hall_down floor 3 (key f = floor index 2 in hall_down keys) and cab floor 3 on elev1. The cab forces elev1 upward; hall_down is the order we test.
SX-B Step 2: Wait for elev1 to start moving upward.
SX-B Step 3: Verify first door-open at floor 3.

SX-B Step 4: Verify second door-open at floor 3 — proves HallDown was NOT cleared on the first pass (Direction::Up preserved). Bug: second door-open never happens because stop() corrupted direction to Stop.
SX-B complete: arrive_at_floor does not corrupt direction at boundary floors.

scenarios.name: SX-A: Bug Verification — Stop Direction Clears Both Hall Orders
scenarios.description: Verifies that when an elevator is already idle at a floor and gets assigned that floor (Direction::Stop path), it does NOT clear both HallUp and HallDown simultaneously. The elevator must open its door twice: once to clear HallUp, and a second time to clear HallDown.

steps.message: Step 1: Move elev1 to floor 1 via cab so it is idle there.
Step 2: Now inject hall_up and hall_down at floor 1. Elevator is already there (Direction::Stop path).
SX-A complete: Stop-direction clear-order serves one direction per door-open.
